title: The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder
population: People with stimulant use disorder, intoxication, or withdrawal
outcomes: Withdrawal, use disorder treatment, psychiatric complications, harm reduction
finding: Provides current management recommendations; contingency management is a primary treatment component and post-acute symptoms may require care.
limitations: Guideline recommendations inherit heterogeneous evidence and are not direct proof for every substance or outcome.

title: Clinical management of psychostimulant withdrawal: review of the evidence
population: People withdrawing from methamphetamine or cocaine
outcomes: Symptoms, trajectory, biomedical and behavioral treatments
finding: Organizes withdrawal into acute and protracted phases and concludes that medication evidence remains limited.
limitations: Primarily methamphetamine and cocaine; not a systematic review focused on non-methamphetamine amphetamine.

title: Treatment for amphetamine withdrawal
outcomes: Withdrawal symptoms, completion, craving, adverse events
finding: Four small randomized trials with 125 participants did not establish a routinely effective medication.
limitations: Very small, old, heterogeneous evidence base; amineptine is not a practical current option.

title: Pharmacological treatment for methamphetamine withdrawal: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
outcomes: Discontinuation, global state, withdrawal, craving, safety
finding: Nine RCTs with 242 participants yielded low or very-low certainty evidence and no convincing routinely effective medication.
limitations: Small trials, high risk of bias, limited safety reporting, predominantly male samples.

title: The nature, time course and severity of methamphetamine withdrawal
outcomes: Withdrawal severity, sleep, appetite, mood, anxiety, craving
finding: Severity peaked within 24 hours, approached controls by the end of week one, then remained lower during a subacute phase.
limitations: Small inpatient Thai cohort; setting and selection limit generalizability.

title: Withdrawal symptoms in abstinent methamphetamine-dependent subjects
outcomes: Depression, psychosis, craving, withdrawal symptoms
finding: Average depression and psychosis improved rapidly, while craving remained measurable across the five-week observation period.
limitations: Inpatient selection and attrition; methamphetamine-specific.

title: The Stimulant Selective Severity Assessment: A replication and exploratory extension of the Cocaine Selective Severity Assessment
outcomes: Internal consistency, construct validity, factor structure
finding: The scale performed acceptably overall and in cocaine groups but poorly in the primarily methamphetamine-only subgroup.
limitations: Small non-cocaine subgroup and no direct non-methamphetamine amphetamine validation.

title: Amphetamine withdrawal: I. Reliability, validity and factor structure of a measure
outcomes: Reliability, validity, factor structure of the AWQ
finding: Developed a short Amphetamine Withdrawal Questionnaire with initial reliability and validity evidence.
limitations: Older single-setting validation; exact exposure composition and transportability require scrutiny.

title: A placebo-controlled trial of mirtazapine for the management of methamphetamine withdrawal
outcomes: Retention, withdrawal symptoms, insomnia, mood, substance use
finding: No significant treatment differences were observed; recruitment and retention limited power.
limitations: Very small sample and 52% completion of the two-week medication phase.

title: Management of Amphetamine and Methamphetamine Use Disorders: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials
outcomes: Abstinence, use, craving, retention, tolerability
finding: No intervention had moderate- or high-certainty evidence for important improvement across patient-important outcomes.
limitations: Network heterogeneity and mixed amphetamine/methamphetamine populations; withdrawal was not the sole target.

title: Prescription psychostimulants for the treatment of amphetamine-type stimulant use disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials
outcomes: Use, craving, retention, withdrawal, depression, safety
finding: A small craving signal was observed, but main analyses did not show significant improvement in withdrawal, use by urinalysis, or retention.
limitations: High heterogeneity; withdrawal outcome included only 138 participants and was very-low certainty.

title: Comparative efficacy and acceptability of psychosocial interventions for individuals with cocaine and amphetamine addiction: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
follow_up: End of treatment and longest follow-up
outcomes: Abstinence by urinalysis, dropout, duration of abstinence
finding: Contingency management combined with community reinforcement performed best for abstinence and acceptability outcomes.
limitations: Cocaine and amphetamine populations pooled; outcomes concern use and retention, not direct withdrawal relief.

title: Bupropion and Naltrexone in Methamphetamine Use Disorder
population: Adults with moderate or severe methamphetamine use disorder
outcomes: Methamphetamine-negative urine response and safety
finding: The combination produced a higher but still low toxicology-defined response than placebo.
limitations: Primary outcome was use response, not acute withdrawal or comprehensive functional recovery.

title: Mirtazapine for Methamphetamine Use Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial
population: 344 adults with moderate to severe methamphetamine use disorder
outcomes: Days of use, toxicology, depression, insomnia, quality of life, safety
finding: Mirtazapine produced a modest additional reduction in self-reported use days, with no significant secondary-outcome improvements.
limitations: Not an acute-withdrawal trial; adherence was limited and drowsiness, weight gain, and discontinuation were more frequent.

title: Is Naltrexone Effective and Safe for Treating Amphetamine-Type Stimulant Use Disorder? A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
population: Adults with amphetamine-type stimulant use disorder
outcomes: Use, retention, craving, safety
finding: Standalone naltrexone did not show a clear benefit over placebo; certainty was low or very low.
limitations: Small evidence base and not withdrawal-specific.

title: ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline for Stimulant Use Disorder Management: Commentary on Research Priorities
population: Stimulant use disorder research and care
outcomes: Implementation and research gaps
finding: Highlights gaps in contingency management implementation, pharmacotherapy, psychosis, harm reduction, and population coverage.
limitations: Commentary rather than primary evidence or systematic synthesis.

title: Evidence-based consensus guidelines for the pharmacological management of substance dependence: Recommendations from the British Association for Psychopharmacology
population: People with substance dependence, including stimulant dependence
outcomes: Pharmacological management and key uncertainties
finding: Concludes that stimulant pharmacotherapy evidence is weak and withdrawal-treatment trials remain small and low quality.
limitations: Consensus guideline rather than a de novo systematic review of every primary study.

title: Amphetamine Withdrawal: II. A Placebo-Controlled, Randomised, Double-Blind Study of Amineptine Treatment
outcomes: AWQ reversed vegetative symptoms, global state, discontinuation
finding: Reported benefit on reversed vegetative symptoms and global state, creating a historical positive signal.
limitations: Small older trial of amineptine, a drug no longer approved in many settings and with abuse-liability concerns.

title: Amphetamine withdrawal: affective state, sleep patterns, and MHPG excretion
design: Small physiological and clinical observational study
population: People withdrawing after prolonged amphetamine abuse
outcomes: Depression, EEG sleep, urinary MHPG
finding: Withdrawal depression tracked changes in MHPG excretion and REM-related sleep measures.
limitations: Very small historical study with dated methods and limited generalizability.

title: Amphetamine withdrawal and sleep disturbance
design: Hospital observational sleep study with controls
population: Amphetamine users after hospital admission and withdrawal
outcomes: Sleep duration, night waking, daytime sleep, variability
finding: Initial oversleeping shifted to reduced and disturbed sleep toward the end of week one, persisting through day 20.
limitations: Historical study, limited sample reporting in accessible abstract, sleep-specific outcome.

title: Self detoxication by amphetamine dependent patients: a pilot study
outcomes: Withdrawal symptoms, coping, relapse, treatment seeking
finding: Eighty-six percent reported significant withdrawal symptoms after stopping amphetamine.
limitations: Retrospective self-report, selected treatment sample, no prospective symptom measurement.

title: Amphetamine and phenmetrazine addiction: physiological abnormalities in the abstinence syndrome
population: People dependent on amphetamine or phenmetrazine
follow_up: Up to 3–8 weeks for sleep normalization
outcomes: EEG sleep abnormalities during abstinence
finding: Marked REM-related abnormalities appeared after withdrawal and normalized over several weeks when drugs remained withheld.
limitations: Six participants, mixed stimulant exposure, historical methods and terminology.
